root_causes.description: The shipping service exhibits a severe server-side latency anomaly (p99 ~4952ms vs ~2ms for healthy leaf services) with zero errors, normal CPU (0.001 cores) and memory (~12.5MB), and no pod crashes. Its only downstream dependency, quote, responds in ~2ms, so the delay originates inside shipping itself (e.g., injected latency in the request path), not from resource pressure or a failing dependency.

evidence.observed_value: p99_latency mean=3793.6ms, p50=4940ms, p99=4952.034ms, max=4952.857ms during incident window
evidence.expected_baseline: p99_latency < 20ms (peer leaf services quote/cart/currency at 1.98ms, email 4.97ms)

cpu_usage mean=0.001, max=0.001 cores — no CPU stress

error_rate=0.000 across entire window — pure latency, no failures
20 traces, 0 errors, p95_duration=106206ms; top traces 8cfef1499a066f07 (13262ms), 7d58d469c7e44054 (8983ms), 99088ae095c2590a (7212ms) — all 'ok' status but multi-second durations
Only routine 'Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource' events; no OOMKilled, BackOff, or crash events

root_causes.description: Checkout's p99 (~9950ms) is roughly 2x shipping's p99 (~4952ms) because checkout invokes shipping twice per order. All other checkout dependencies (cart 1.98ms, payment 1.98ms, currency 1.98ms, email 4.97ms, product-catalog ~17ms) are healthy, confirming the latency is fully attributable to the shipping dependency.

evidence.observed_value: payment p99_latency=1.98ms — other checkout dependencies healthy (cart 1.98ms, currency 1.98ms, email 4.97ms, product-catalog 17.0ms)
checkout → cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog; shipping → quote
evidence.expected_baseline: Dependency graph confirms shipping is the only slow checkout dependency

root_causes.description: Frontend p99 (~9121ms) is downstream propagation of the checkout/shipping latency; frontend itself is not faulted — it simply waits on checkout, which waits on shipping.

remediation_steps: Remove the latency fault in the shipping service: check for chaos-experiment/flagd feature-flag latency injection or an artificial sleep in the shipping request handler and disable it.
Add a strict client-side timeout (e.g., 500ms-1s) in checkout for shipping RPC calls so a slow shipping service cannot inflate checkout/frontend p99 to ~10s.
Implement a circuit breaker / retry-with-backoff in checkout for shipping calls to fail fast during latency degradation.
Add a p99 latency SLO alert on shipping (threshold ~50ms) to catch this fault class earlier than the frontend-level watchdog.
After mitigation, verify shipping p99 returns to ~2ms and checkout/frontend p99 recover to sub-second baselines.
